### 73 — Chest straightening: root cause of the bib collapse found and fixed (UV-seam fold → Laplacian relaxation); clamp still held out by the front-digit render gate

**Order acted on:** author priority 1 (straight chest) left open by entry 72 —
"re-enable together with the bib_mask re-anchor".

**Diagnosis (build logs, `scratch/iter-73/build*.log`).** Entry 72's "atlas
share" collapse was NOT a mask problem (`bib_mask` already keys on the
segment frame; the clamp moved only 242 verts, front sign never flips). It is
a UV-seam fold: the snap clamp is C0 but not C1, so the surface creases along
the moved/unmoved boundary, `smart_project` (angle_limit 66°) cuts seams
there, and the seam-spanning-triangle skip in the plate sampler drops the
front bib island's samples **660 → 360** (bins 15 vs the back's 37).

**Fix (kept, `blender/build_body.py`, call still DISABLED):** a local
Laplacian relaxation after the clamp — 2 iterations over the moved verts +
vertex rings (w 0.45/0.30) — smooths the fold so the unwrap stays intact.
Full enablement measured green on every BUILD and BODY gate:

- chest gates: 242 verts clamped, front-line deviation **0.0 mm** (limit 20);
- front bib plate samples **360 → 700** (back 640), ink fraction **0.280**
  front / 0.178 back, bins 35 vs 37 — island fragmentation gone;
- `body.spec` front-back blue delta **0.040** (gate 0.03; was 0.010 with the
  clamp on in entry 72); unit 76/76, golden 30/30 (physics untouched).

A first relaxation variant smoothed the whole torso and tripped the suit
NM-variance gate (6.14 < 6.30); scoping it to the fold neighbourhoods fixed
that without losing the unwrap.

**Why the clamp is still not enabled:** with the clamp on, the RENDER gate
`bib-number.spec` front navyFrac goes to **0.0000** (back unchanged 0.1766;
entry 72 shipped a marginal 0.0362). Probes (`scratch/iter-73/probe_bib.js`,
12-step alpha sweep, and an auto-faced variant of the spec) show the front
"30" does not read from ANY quadrant of the rest pose — entry 72's front pass
was measuring a sliver at a stale hard-coded alpha 0 that no longer faces the
chest. `shots/figure_front.png` (and figure/figure_side) contain zero navy
pixels this build. So the front-digit readability defect PRE-DATES the clamp;
the clamp only removes the marginal sliver that used to pass.

**Verification:** assets/bumps REVERTED to HEAD (build not shipped);
unit 76/76, golden 30/30, body 4/4 + bib-number + rig 15 passed on the
reverted tree. Scratch in `/home/justin/aerial-agents/scratch/iter-73/`
(build logs, probes).

**Open / next:** (1) real front-plate framing: make `bib-number.spec`
auto-face like `figure_front` (implemented and demonstrated this iteration,
reverted with the experiment — it correctly measures 0.0049 at the true
chest) AND make `look.spec`'s figure_front framing robust (an ASCII render of
the current `figure_front.png` shows a wide shot, not the 2.4 m closeup —
the quadrant bib-blue score is dominated by sky at that radius); then
(2) flip the `straighten_chest(body)` call, ASSET_V bump, one rebuild — the
geometry side is ready and gated.

**Open questions for the reviewer:** (1) the front "30" currently does not
read at the canonical cameras at all (pre-existing; entry 72's pass was a
sliver at a stale alpha) — approve fixing the bib/figure_front framing as its
own iteration, with the clamp enabled in the same rebuild? (2) d/b breadth
convention question from entry 72 still open (SOFT gate logs 1.20 bare-trunk

### 71 — The five-times-ordered 15-minute sky colour slice finally landed:

gradient + the two `skyMat` colours. No assets, ASSET_V unchanged, engine
untouched.

**Change:** the old gradient mixed zenith→horizon with `pow(1.0−y, 2.4)`,
which painted a ~20°-tall pale band over every low-elevation view — that was
the wash the reviewer kept measuring. Now the haze band completes by
y = 0.035 (~2°) via `1.0 − smoothstep(0.008, 0.035, y)`, so the saturated
blue reaches to within ~2–5° of the tree line. Colours: zenith
(0.16, 0.34, 0.66) → shipped (0.13, 0.29, 0.58) after gate calibration;
horizon (0.50, 0.60, 0.85) → (0.60, 0.72, 0.88); cloud coverage threshold
briefly tightened then restored to the original `smoothstep(0.52, 0.66, f)`
with density 0.92 → 0.85. One shader-edit bug caught by the spec's own
signal (a dropped `float f = _fbm(...)` line killed the dome → flat
clearColor: sun == zenith, whiteFrac 0) and fixed.

**Verification:** `sky.spec` 3/3 green, all gates — zenith lum 0.574 ∈
[0.10, 0.60], zenith r−b −0.309 (gate ≤ −0.12), sky-band r−b −0.319 (NEW

only); `look` 1/1, shots regenerated; `review-measure` unchanged on terrain:
corridor_vs_flankNear −0.0244, seam skyFrac 0.175, shadow drop 0.075, face

### 89 — Crash roll-to-the-flat phase with hard gates + negative control (NEXT.md, deleted in this commit)

**Task (reviewer 2026-08-29 02:55):** the body stopped ~1.2 s after the crash trigger wherever
it was (entry 84's re-verification only passed because the spec never asked for the roll).
Required: tumble ≤ 1.0 s → rigid `roll` down the slope (friction ≈ 2–3 m/s²) while the local
slope is ≥ 10° → freeze on the < 10° flat ON the snow; skis eject; hard gates on rest position,
motion time, support, joint speed; a negative control with the roll disabled that must FAIL.

**What changed (all renderer-side, `engine/` untouched):**
- `_crashRagdollStep`: `slide` → `roll`. At the 1.0 s freeze the mean tumble velocity is
  replaced by a downhill momentum seed of 15 m/s (the crash impact speed; the PBD verlet
  damping under-reports it — without the seed the frozen crumple crawls at the floor speed and
  never reaches the flat). On slope ≥ 10°: net decel 3.0 m/s² with a 4 m/s floor (never stalls
  mid-slope); on the < 10° flat: friction decel 7.7 m/s² to the 0.1 m/s freeze. The roll stays
  rigid (every part gets the same delta — joint angular speed ~1e-13 rad/s, far under the
  90°/s gate) and rides the slope plane as before.
- **Settle-while-rolling:** propped parts are lowered at 0.3 m/s toward their contact plane
  during the roll (segment-end ≤ 0.6 m/s ⇒ joint rate stays under 90°/s) with a hard-stick
  re-projection, so the resting pose lies ON the snow (support 11 points, max point 0.151 m
  above the snow) instead of propped at 0.76 m in the frozen crumple. `['torsoTop','neck']`
  and `['neck','headTop']` moved into the HARD stick list (the descent left a 5 cm neck-gap
  residual on soft sticks). At the stop: a 10-pass Gauss-Seidel relax zeroes residuals, and the
  prev-reset moved AFTER it (the spray instrument otherwise read phantom post-stop creep).
- Negative control: `window._crashRollDisabled` (set by the spec before the crash) restores the
  old iter-47 exponential stop.
- `window._crashRollOutZ` (OUTRUN_Z) exposed for the rest-position gate.

**Gates (all hard, `tests/drive/crash-ragdoll.spec.js` rewritten):** state machine reaches
`stopped`; total motion restAt(sim) in 2–5 s (sim time — wall clock in the SwiftShader suite
runs 2–4× slow, the old wall gates were the wrong instrument); rest ≥ 60 % of trigger→roll-out
AND rest slope < 10°; ≥ 3 support points within 5 cm; no point > 0.6 m above the snow; worst
penetration ≤ 5 cm; joint gaps ≤ 2 cm; skis on the surface; joint angular speed ≤ 90°/s from
the freeze; ≥ 3 s of exactly-0 post-stop samples; no legacy solids. New `shots/crash_rest.png`
from a geometric side camera at the rest position.

**Verification (measured, default world, SwiftShader):** tumble ends t=1.0 s (sim); roll start
z=36.2, rollOutZ=63.70, restZ=68.80 → 118 % of trigger→roll-out at 0.0° slope; restAt=4.79 s
(gate 2–5); support=11, maxAbove=0.151 m; joint angular speed 4e-13 rad/s; NEGATIVE CONTROL
rests at 9 % / 40.0° and FAILS the gate (test asserts the failure) — `2 passed`.
`npm run test:unit` 78/78, `npm run test:golden` 30/30 after re-capture, `look` green; shots
regenerated (`scene/figure/figure_front/figure_side/face` unchanged in character, new
`crash_rest.png` inspected: athlete resting on the flat beside the netting).

**Golden rebaseline (ADR-0005, display change — crash is ADR-0002 display):** 13 aerial
traces contain the crash tail in their digest (every scenario that lands badly), so the roll
changes `frame[495+]` head/torso nodes by ~1–5 cm in those scenarios; all 30 re-captured with
`node tests/golden/capture.js` (30/30 clean). Physics scenarios (trampoline/pool) byte-stable.

**Open questions for the reviewer:**
1. The roll's momentum seed (15 m/s) and decel (3.0 / 7.7 m/s²) are tuned to the default
   world's ~28 m landing slope to land inside the 2–5 s / ≥ 60 % gates. Custom worlds with
   much longer landings will roll proportionally farther — is per-world tuning acceptable
   later, or should the parameters derive from the impact speed measured at the trigger?
2. NEXT's "friction deceleration ≈ 2–3 m/s²" is ambiguous (net vs friction magnitude). I read
   it as NET 3.0 m/s² on the slope; gravity would otherwise accelerate the mass and blow the
   2–5 s envelope. Confirm the reading.
3. The 2–5 s gate is enforced in simulation time (probe clock). In a real 60 fps browser
   sim ≈ wall, so the author-visible behaviour matches; in the SwiftShader suite wall time
   stretches 2–4×. Flag if you want a wall-clock gate in a non-SwiftShader run instead.

### 104 — NEXT item 2: ridge flatness ROOT-CAUSED (elevation keying put all
bands on the hidden back slope); snowline remapped + contrast raised;
look.spec timeout fix

Eye confirmation of 103's slice FAILED: `scene.png`/`inrun.png`/`kicker.png`
still read as smooth pale-blue gradients — no rock banding, no jittered
snowline, no tree-line band. Root cause (not contrast): the ridge texture
bands key on elevation `v = (y − valleyFloorY) / RIDGE_SNOWLINE_M`, but crest
heights are 29/52/77 m (near/mid/far above the valley floor), so at
SNOWLINE 45 m every visible face sat above `snowEdge` 0.60+jitter and clamped
into the snowfield band; the forest (v<0.42) and rock (0.42–0.60) bands only
existed on the hidden away-from-valley back slope.

Fix: `RIDGE_SNOWLINE_M` 45 → **80 m** (`game.js`) so the visible faces carry
the bands — near crests v≈0.36 (forest/tree-line), mid ≈0.65 (rock/snow edge
with jittered snowline), far/back pure snowfield — and snowfield rock
outcrops strengthened in `makeRidgeSurface` ((d−0.52)·2.2 → (d−0.50)·3.2).
`ridges3d.spec.js` 2/2 green (flat-curtain negative control still fails);
golden 30/30 (headless stub-canvas path untouched); unit 78/78.

(measured 5.1–5.2 m for 12+ stills at 1100×850 across three runs; the
regenerated shots WERE written each time before the timeout) —
`tests/drive/playwright.config.js` timeout 300_000 → 420_000; look now
**passes in 4.1 m**.

Post-fix measurement (`scene.png` ridge band, rows 5–30% of frame):
meanLum 0.638, mean horizontal gradient 0.030 (normalized), gradP90 25/255 —
texture is now present (visible facet mottling + faint grey rock patches on
the mid ridge in `kicker.png`) but STILL WEAK by eye; the tree-line band does

coordinate `u` (0 = crest) into the band keying so the bands are placed on

actually on-camera in these framings.

### 114 — cone-peak re-land ATTEMPTED, NOT LANDED — two decoupled blockers measured (darkU dose–response knife edge; ridges3d mask collapse with a contradictory signature); tree reverted to HEAD, all suites green

**Task:** entry 113's open item 1 — re-land the peaks with the shaded-flank
fix. Implementation was restored from
`~/aerial-agents/scratch/iter-113/game.peaks.js` (11 `pk_body_*`, band UV,
/55 v-clamp) and the flank fix was attacked with `peakMat.emissiveColor`
lifts (no albedo/fog/UV changes). **Nothing committed: game.js and the
golden traces are back at HEAD (`43b571b`), verified green.**

**Measured dose–response (look.spec FACEDISC, swiftshader; gates: front
darkU > 0.015, back darkU < 0.015):**

| peakMat emissive (cool white) | front darkU | back darkU | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (entry 113 state) | pass | 0.3926 | back FAIL |
| 0.10 | 0.3443 | 0.3822 | back FAIL — the flank base is far below 0.30, not marginally below |
| 0.20 | 0.0505 | 0.1418 | both still FAIL |
| 0.25 | 0.0078 | 0.0327 | back passes, front FAILS — bloom (pipeline threshold 0.88) smears the brightened peaks into the FRONT close-up and washes out the goggle lens |

So the fix is a knife edge: back needs ≈ 0.24, front breaks at 0.25 — and
0.10 barely moved back darkU (−0.01), meaning the dark region is NOT uniformly
flank at ~0.3 luminance; large parts of it are much darker (likely the
between-cone gaps / bump-shaded facets seen sky-through). Emissive alone
cannot decouple the two gates. Next candidates (cheapest first): (a) raise
the emissive AND raise `dofPipeline.bloomThreshold` — but DoF/pipeline is the
Opus lane (standing rule), needs their sign-off; (b) drop `peakMat.bumpTexture`
+ geometry-side: lower the side-range peaks below the back close-up's upper
third (needs a framing-angle calc); (c) reviewer call on the face-back gate
excluding the background (queued below).

**Second blocker — ridges3d contrast mask collapses to 0 whenever the peaks
exist** (`maskFrac 0` in BOTH the positive and the fogged negative control,
i.e. the gate fails "ridges in frame", and even the negative control loses
its signal). Signature measured with a throwaway probe spec in the Playwright
environment:
- Peaks ARE rendered and DO change the frame: hiding `pk_body_*` alone moves
  311,059 px (8.3% of frame) and mean frame luminance A(all)=0.669 →
  B(peaks hidden)=0.742 → C(peaks+ridges hidden)=0.767 — per-channel means
  differ by 9–23/255, far above the mask's d ≥ 12 threshold.
- Yet the spec's withR/without differencing returns 0 differing pixels. The
  probe's A-vs-B order (hide peaks first) vs the spec's (hide ridges+peaks in
  one step) is the only structural difference found; the discrepancy is NOT
  resolved. Suspects: a per-pixel vs per-mean error in my probe (the mask
  might be true-zero only when BOTH backdrop layers hide in the same grab),
  or a readPixels double-buffer effect tied to the peaks' extra 512² ridge
  surface texture allocation. Widening the spec mask to `ridge_` +
  `pk_body_\d+` did NOT lift maskFrac — needs a fresh iteration with
  screenshots instead of inference.
- At reverted HEAD: ridges3d 4/4, mask 0.1214/0.498/0.165 (unchanged from
  entry 110's numbers).

### 117 — P10 free-look camera LANDED — orbit in ready state / after a stop / once the crash ragdoll rests / in replay, terrain clamp, Dvorak-aware WASD, launch keys preserved

Reviewer order for 117 (Fable, 2026-08-29 17:30) followed. No `docs/NEXT.md` this
iteration; no athlete/pipeline files touched (standing rules respected).

**What changed (`game.js`, +~110 lines):**
- `_freeLookAllowed()` (near the fpCamera block): `(readyState && readyTurnT === 0.0) || state.stopped || (state.crashed && (!crashActive || ragdoll resting)) || replayActive`. Crash case keys off `_ragdollProbe().resting` because `crashActive` deliberately stays true after the rest detector fires (it is only cleared on reset).
- Per-frame toggle in the render loop: entering free-look unlocks wheel zoom (`lowerRadiusLimit 3`, `upperRadiusLimit 80`) and starts the one-time HUD hint; leaving restores the locked follow radius (3/80 → 10/10, `radius = 10`).
- While free-look is active the whole camera-follow block (target y/z, C-key alpha lerp, airborne beta raise) stands down, so a user drag/zoom/pan persists indefinitely; it resumes the moment the next run starts.
- Terrain clamp `_clampCameraAboveTerrain()` every frame on the orbit camera: eye kept ≥ 1.0 m over `terrainRootY(z) - FOOT_OFFSET` by capping beta (`acos((minY − target.y)/radius)`, clamped to the 0.05..π−0.05 limits); if the entire orbit sphere is under the clamp the target is raised first. Try/catch-guarded; runs in follow mode too (harmless there — verified golden 30/30).
- WASD nudge, layout-aware via the existing `_keyIsLetter` convention (the key that TYPES the letter fires, matching the help text): A/D orbit alpha ±0.12 (shift ±0.04), W/S radius ×0.94/÷0.94. Separate listener gated on free-look, so no game key is shadowed — ArrowUp still starts the run mid-orbit.
- HUD hint line appended for 5 s after the first activation: "drag to look around · wheel or W/S zoom · A/D pan".
*Instruments:* `window._freeLookProbe()` → `{active, alpha, beta, radius, gap}` (gap = eye height above the snow surface); `window._freeLookCam()` for the specs.

### 137 — tree-shadow "dirt smudges" root-caused (live cone wedges; the baked
lightmap is dead) + `bake_lightmap.py` tree-occluder groundwork

**Order acted on:** the Seventh-Opus-merge order for 129–145, item (c)
remainder — review-125 scene note: "dark under-canopy shadow streaks on the
flank read as dirt smudges rather than tree shadows". Items (a) Snowing and
the B-net half of (c) already landed (129/131 and 133). No `docs/NEXT.md`.

**Investigation (measured, not guessed):**
- `scene.png` by eye: the left-flank streaks are long, uniform, featureless
  grey wedges detached from any crown shape, and the near trees show no
  contact shadow at their bases.
- Root cause: every tree shadows through ONE solid 6-sided cone per tree
  (`treeShadowProxy`, `game.js` ~4330 — a SwiftShader frame-time stand-in for
  alpha-tested cards in the CSM depth pass, tools/scratch-tree-cost.js: 40 ms
  with cards vs 109.6→149.9 ms splice test). A cone's shadow at the ~32° sun
  IS a featureless wedge — the smudge read is the mechanism, not the tuning.
- The static bake cannot currently take over: in a live page
  `window._bakedApplied` is **0** — the 08-25 `terrain_uv2.json` names/vertex
  counts (wInrun/wTable/… 28-mesh era) match no current mesh, so no snow mesh
  receives `terrain_shadow.png` at all. And a fresh bake attempt fails at
  `check_uv_consistency`: `terrainCorridor` now shares vertices across faces
  (smoothed normals) = **2204 per-vertex UV conflicts**, so the sidecar cannot
  represent it. `terrainSkirt`/`terrainBase` (vertical closure walls, new
  since the bake) also fail the old receiver assert.

**Landed (bake groundwork, no game-side change — nothing rendered differs):**
- `blender/bake_lightmap.py`: `add_tree_occluders()` (`--trees`, default
  `blender/trees.json`) adds the forest as alpha-cutout crossed-card
  occluders — per-variant materials using the shipped `tree_*_card_*.png`
  alpha, Transparent→Principled mix, so Cycles path-traces crown-shaped,

### 134 — entry-133 blotch fix: STRATA band map for the peaks and the
mid/far ridges — the dark outcrop/fracture noise read as camouflage
blotches; now layered rock strata

**Order acted on:** entry-133 open question 1 (its by-eye finding: "the dark
bands read as camouflage blotches, not rock" on the UPPER-LEFT RIDGE/PEAK
faces). No `docs/NEXT.md`. No Reviewer feedback beyond the standing rules.

**Root cause (seen in the raster, not guessed):** the peaks and the
mid/far ridges all shared `makeRidgeSurface`'s default map. On the cones one
texture width spans the whole 2π circumference (~130 m), and on the ridge
faces the rock band's `mix(ROCK, DARK, (r−0.55)·0.9)` fractures plus the
snow band's `mix(SNOW, ROCK, (d−0.47)·3.6)` outcrops render as irregular
high-contrast dark blobs — camouflage, not geology.

**Fix (display-only):**
- `render/textures.js` `makeRidgeSurface(..., { strata: true })`: band-edge
  jitter 0.12 → 0.04, snow-band outcrop contrast 3.6 → 1.6, rock-fracture
  dark mix 0.9 → 0.45, plus near-horizontal sediment strata
  `sin(v·2π·9 + small jitter)` mixing ±0.22 rock/dark tones keyed on
  elevation. Default (non-strata) output byte-identical.
- `game.js`: `_ridgeMat` gains a `texOpts` pass-through; `peakMatBase`,
  `matMid`, `matFar` build the strata map (bump strength 2.2); the NEAR
  ridge keeps the full-detail forest map (tree-line strokes read up close).
- `index.html` `game.js?v=51`.

**Verification:** unit **81/81**; golden **30/30** ("30/30 scenarios match
the golden traces", verify.js the last command before this commit —
display-only, no re-capture); `ridges3d.spec` **5/5** twice (with peaks-only,
then with mid/far ridges on strata): peak gate mask 0.053, peak-pixel mean
**0.677** / std **0.0846** (floor 0.05), ridge-only contrast gates and the
fogged negative control still discriminate; `look` **4/4**, shots
regenerated. `scene.png` luminance bands 0–20% **0.663** / 20–35% **0.616** /
35–50% **0.778** (133: 0.661/0.618/0.794 — unchanged within noise). BY EYE
(raster, this session): the mid-left ridge face that was dark-mottled now
reads as smooth layered grey strata; the right-hand cones are pale with

### 133 — review-125 B-net near-post read fixed: the grazing-angle strip was
alpha-culled by mip averaging (cutoff 0.5 → 0.3); new venue-dressing gate
with an in-page negative control

**Order acted on:** reviewer ruling on entry 131 (129–145 order): after 132's
mountains follow-up, the "B-net/canopy notes" — review-125 scene note (2):
"the near-left B-net posts read as a row of floating dark sticks — the net
mesh is invisible at that grazing angle". No `docs/NEXT.md`.

**Root cause (measured, not guessed):** the net tile's rope coverage is
~45% of texels, so the HIGH mip levels average alpha to ~0.45 — below
`alphaCutOff = 0.5` — and the GPU culled the ENTIRE strip once it was small
or oblique enough in screen space for the mips to engage. The face-on far
fence kept full-res texels (binary 0/1 alpha) and survived, which is why
only the near-left side read as bare posts. This session could raster PNGs,
so the defect was confirmed by eye in `shots/scene.png` before the fix
(near-left: posts only; far-right: full net).

**Fix (display-only, one line + comment):** `bnetMat.alphaCutOff`
0.5 → 0.3 (`game.js`). Full-res alpha is unchanged (clearRect + strokes =
0 or 1), so holes near the camera stay identical; only the mip-collapsed
distance case differs. `index.html`: `game.js?v=49` → `?v=50`.

**New gate (`venue-dressing.spec.js` test 5):** from the look.spec scene
framing, hide `bnetStrip_L` and difference the frame (mask = pixels that
changed ≥ 12/255). Measured (SwiftShader): mask **0.0151** at cutoff 0.3,
**0.0092** at 0.4, **0.0039** at the pre-fix 0.5 — monotone in the mip
averaging. Gates: control (cutoff 0.5 set in-page) < 0.007, visible
> max(0.012, 2×control) — ≥ 2× discrimination each way.

**Verification:** venue-dressing **5/5**; unit **81/81** (fail 0); golden
**30/30** (verify.js the last command before this commit — display-only
change, no re-capture); `look` **4/4**, shots regenerated. `scene.png` by
eye after: the near-left fence now shows net between its posts down the
in-run; the far fence is unchanged.

**Canopy half of the note (review-125 item 3), by eye at this tip:** the
tree shadows on the flank in the regenerated `scene.png` read as soft
canopy blobs, acceptable at this sun angle — no smudge defect visible in
this view, so no change made. What DOES read as dark smudges is the
UPPER-LEFT RIDGE/PEAK faces: iter-132's rock band map shows as irregular
dark blotches on the pale ridge waves rather than structured strata (the
132 open question 1 by-eye check). Not touched this iteration.

**Open questions for the reviewer:** (1) confirm the 132 peak banding by
eye — in `scene.png` the dark bands read as camouflage blotches, not rock;
options if you agree: lower the band-map contrast on the peak materials,
or stretch the snowline divisor so bands are wider/stratified; (2) the

### 127 — crash determinism COMPLETE: the post-stop rendered spike was the
freeze transition itself; park + world-matrix freeze now land in the same
step that detects rest — crash-ragdoll fully green incl. negative controls

**What changed (carried from 126; display-only, `engine/` untouched):**
Root cause found by instrumenting the spec's TAIL sampler with the torso
node's `isWorldMatrixFrozen` flag: on failing runs the spike sample read
`frozen=true`, i.e. the spike was NOT a mystery external writer — it was the
first rendered frame AFTER the iter-126 freeze engaged. The freeze ran at the
START of `_crashRagdollStep` one step AFTER `R.resting` was set, so that one
frame rendered the driver chain on the engine root the machine had kept
integrating past the out-run (drifting/falling) — a ~0.37 m one-sample jump
(measured 3.2–4.6 m/s) exactly at the stop boundary, which `settledTail`
(the samples right after the first `resting` sample) always caught.

Fix: park the display root AND freeze the world matrices of the root + all
driver nodes at the END of the same step in which rest was detected — the
driver locals are freshly written there and the root is positioned at the
capture, so the transition frame already renders the parked matrix
(`_crashRagdollStep`, `game.js`). `R._frozen`/`R._park` guard one-shot
execution; the per-frame park block and the `onBeforeRenderObservable`
re-park from iter 126 stay. The next-run reset in the crash teardown
unfreezes the whole chain so normal per-frame matrix updates resume
(skis' rotationQuaternion clearing and visibility restore untouched).

**Verification:** `node --check` clean; unit **81/81**; golden **30/30**
(`node tests/golden/verify.js` last command before the commit — no
re-capture: no physics or display-census change); crash-ragdoll **3/3**
including BOTH negative controls (roll-less rest gate fails as required;
limp excursion exceeds the 38° gate — probe alive throughout, so the
entry-126 mid-run `_crashRagdollStep` exception class is gone; a temporary
diagnostic line that threw post-rest and killed the ragdoll was caught by
exactly these controls and removed before commit). Zero TAIL samples on the
green run; in-page 12 s post-rest probe: zero jumps > 2 cm, frozen=true.
Two prior solo runs of the same build (before the freeze was relocated)
still spiked — consistent with the transition explanation.

### 123 — entry-121 never-stopped crash residual FIXED: two roll-phase bugs

root-slide lag compensation; crash-ragdoll 3/3, look 4/4

Root-caused in `game.js` `_crashRagdollStep`'s roll phase, two real bugs that
the swallowed try/catch (line ≈7981) hid:
1. The steep branch referenced `_vH0`, declared only in the sibling `else`
   block — a ReferenceError on EVERY roll frame on the steep. The catch set
   `_crashErr` and nulled the ragdoll, so once the freeze landed on the
   landing slope the machine silently died and `resting` never fired. This
   WAS the never-stopped run (and why the two negative controls always
   passed — their `_crashRollDisabled` branch precedes the steep branch).
2. The flat branch computed friction `_k` but never applied it
   (`R.slideV *= _k` missing) — a second never-stopped path on the flat.
   Both fixed; `node --check` passes (it cannot catch a TDZ read).
3. Rendered-tail drift: after rest the write-back projected the frozen pose
   through the root position captured at step entry while the engine kept
   sliding the root — measured rendered torso speed 0.109 m/s post-stop vs
   the 0.06 gate. Fix: while the pose is rigid (every phase after tumble)
   the frozen world points are translated by the root's per-step delta
   before projection; a solo probe then reads exactly 0.000 for every
   post-stop sample.
4. Spec instrument (not the model): the "settled" tail gate now measures
   from `firstStopped+1` — `tSpeed[i]` spans sample i−1, which was still

declared — the old instant stop left `maxAbove` 0.612–0.615 m vs the 0.6 m

### 179 — NEXT.md item 4: HT#22 fang peak root-caused (ridge sheet END edge, not a cone) + end-taper fix with mesh-space gate

**What changed.**
- **Diagnosis (hide-mesh probe, per-mesh):** the author's `author_tooth2` claw
  is NOT a cone peak and NOT texture. Hiding `pk_body_*` leaves the claw;
  hiding `ridge_*` removes it; per-sheet isolation pins it on **`ridge_ahead`**
  (present-by-class on every ridge sheet). Cause: `_ridgeMesh` builds an OPEN
  heightfield sheet whose crest runs at full height right up to the last 6 m
  column and then drops to below the valley floor — a free ~40 m wall. Seen
  nearly edge-on past the other ridges, that end wall projects as a dark
  hooked sliver floating over the pale cone peaks: the "fang".
- **Fix (game.js, `_ridgeMesh`):** the crest now fades to ground over
  `RIDGE_END_TAPER_FRAC` = 0.14 of the run at BOTH lateral ends
  (smoothstep), so each sheet end meets the ground and cannot project a free
  edge. `?fangkeepends=1` restores the unfaded ends — the negative control.
  No engine/, no athlete, no DoF, no asset, no ASSET_V change (no assets
  regenerated). Display geometry only — golden physics untouched (30/30
  without re-capture).
- **New gate `tests/drive/peak-overhang.spec.js`:** mesh-space, reads the LIVE
  Babylon vertex data of every `ridge_*` sheet: the crest row (j=0) may step
  at most **12 m per 6 m column**. The unfaded fang end steps ~24 m in one
  column (crest → floor); the tapered ends step ≤ ~6 m, as does the sine
  silhouette itself (max sine step ≈ amp·f·6 m ≈ 5.7 m).

**Verification numbers.**
- peak-overhang 2/2: positive gate green on all 8 ridge sheets; negative
  control (`?fangkeepends=1`) FAILS the gate as required (worst step > 12 m).
- unit 81/81; golden 30/30 (no traces moved); ridges3d 5/5 (depth ≥ 21% and
  textured-material gates unaffected by the taper); look 6/6, shots
  regenerated; `shots/scene.png` inspected by eye — the hooked claw is gone,
  the skyline is clean layered ridges and cones.
- Shelved experiment: a render-space "sky-below-mountain" pixel overhang
  detector. Two dead ends are recorded so nobody re-treads them: (1) with the
  real gradient sky, horizon haze sits within ~5 RGB points of the snowfield

### 191 — NEXT.md 5a-NEW(i), #26 root cause SPLIT by render probe: front hole = skinned-inverted faces (culled backfaces), back hole = a real geometric gap (survives culling off); fix scoped for 192

**Route.** Work slot on NEXT.md 5a-NEW(i) (the #26 mesh-side abdomen/hip fix,
the carried red). The Blender mesh surgery itself did not land this slot — the
slot went to the proof-first probe that 189's open question 1 asked for, and it
changed the fix design. No source, asset, gate, engine, or ASSET_V change
(probe builds went to scratch; assets byte-identical to committed v76).

**The probe (scratch spec, deleted after measurement).** The `leg-watertight`
measurement camera path, run three ways on the shipped build: (a) as shipped;
(b) after `bone.returnToRest()` on every skeleton bone; (c) after
`backFaceCulling=false` on all three athleteBody materials. Colour sampling
checked what the "background" inside the holes actually is.

**Findings (all measured, 1280x720 athlete-only frames).**
1. **The `returnToRest` leg of the probe is INCONCLUSIVE**: the game's pose loop
   re-poses the skeleton every frame, so side/back renders came back
   byte-identical posed vs "rest". 189's "skinned separation" read therefore
   needed a different discriminator.
2. **FRONT (the byte-stable hole, 52 px at x 674–679, y 324–338 — reproduced
   identical in 189, 190, and twice this slot): it is CULLED BACKFACES.** With
   `backFaceCulling=false` the hole is exactly 0. So at that spot the posed
   skin has degenerate/flipped triangles that Babylon backface-culls away —
   the session-23 belly-vertex class (`upperArmR` dragging lower-belly skin,
   the fan-of-shards essay in build_body.py). Fix class: weight/locality
   repair at the abdomen band, or a rest-space geometry overlap; NOT a rim cap.
3. **BACK: the hole is a REAL GEOMETRIC GAP.** With culling off the hole
   PERSISTS (324 px at x 647–672, y 330–365, plus 27 px more appearing
   elsewhere) — with culling off, a closed mesh cannot show background at all,
   so genuine background visibility there means either an open boundary the
   rest-space census missed or pose-driven separation of mesh islands at the
   back hip. Winding is also excluded (the gap survives culling off; an
   inside-out patch would have been healed by it). Paint is excluded by
   colour: the clear colour is pale sky (189, 209, 217), the isBg threshold is
   sum-diff < 40, and the suit's darkest pixel in the band is (21, 21, 23) —
   the hole pixels match the sky, not dark paint.
4. **The gate is NONDETERMINISTIC on side/back between runs**: side measured
   84 px (2 holes, y 234–253) in one run and 0 px in another; back measured
   296 px in 4 narrow vertical slits in one run and 324 px in 1 in another —
   all above the hip row, all in the same defect class. FRONT alone was
   byte-stable across every run (which is why 190's "byte-identical"
   reproduction held). Suspected cause: the ready-state idle sway changing the
   posed frame between measurements. This matters for any future
   "reproduces byte-identical" claim about side/back and for the gate's false
   GREEN risk (side CAN read 0). An instrument-side fix candidate: freeze the
   athlete's pose (or pause the idle sway) inside the measurement, and/or
   measure max-over-N-frames. Not landed this slot (spec change = gate change;
   needs a ruling).

**Fix design for 192 (scoped, evidence-based, in order).**
1. Back gap: in the build, find the posed-pose separation at the back hip
   (candidates: the torso-shell bottom rim vs the thigh-tube top rim, or a
   pelvis-sheet edge) and WIDEN THE REST OVERLAP so no gameplay pose can open
   it (bind law: the overlap is rest geometry — it must live in the BINDS).
   Probe aid: a `scene.pickWithRay` through the hole pixel to identify exactly
   which surface pair brackets the gap.
2. Front hole: after the back fix, re-measure; if it persists, repair the
   offending belly-region weights (the locality essay's own machinery), with
   `backFaceCulling=false` as the diagnostic that the inversion class is gone.
3. Instrument: propose freezing the pose in `leg-watertight.spec.js` for
   determinism (ruling requested below).

**Verification.** unit **81/81**; golden **30/30** (no change shipped);
`leg-watertight` solo: legacy leg gate green, full-body gate RED with front
52 px (byte-identical to 189/190) — the carried red stands, now with a split
root cause; `look` **6/6**, shots regenerated. ASSET_V unchanged at 76.
Scratch in `/home/justin/aerial-agents/scratch/iter-191/` (probe glb, island
census, probe spec copies — reviewer sweeps).

**Open questions for the reviewer.**
1. May `leg-watertight.spec.js` freeze the athlete's idle sway (or measure
   max-over-N frames) for determinism? Side/back currently flake between 0 and
   ~84 px across runs, which is both a false-green risk and it makes

2. Given the split root cause, is the 192 unit "back-gap overlap fix + front

| config | frames (live) | worst heel lift | worst airborne |

**Root-cause note on why the author's lift is not reproducing:** the boot–ski
pin at `game.js:9790` places the shins on the ski line unconditionally every
frame (its `w = tuck·(1−armRaise)` weight only scales the cuff lean), so even

(`applyPose` gets `max(tuck, offAxisVisualTuck)` while the pin reads
`tuckAmount` only), analog partial tuck — all measure seated on HEAD. The
historic defect appears only when the pin is skipped entirely, exactly what
the negative control injects (252 mm mid-blend airborne). The suspected
blind-spot mechanisms (off-axis visual tuck, pike-zeroed pin weight) are now
permanently covered rather than assumed safe.

**Coverage limits (stated, not hidden):** the gamepad config stubs
`navigator.getGamepads` and drives the game's real polling/bridge path
(RT→tuckTarget, X→ArrowUp); it cannot exercise a physical pad's stick
arm-lateral path. Pool-dive/trampoline modes are out of the sweep's z-window.

six configs, name it and it joins the gate.

### 199 — #25 knee band, part 1: the KNEE BRIDGE — one continuous garment tube across the knee (silhouette bump 14.0/20.9 → 2.7/1.7 mm), instrument + hard gate with firing negative control; ONE carried red: leg-watertight side (classification flip of the pre-existing knee-crook see-through)

**What changed** (`blender/build_body.py`, new `KNEE BRIDGE` pass inside `suit_shell` after the
existing smoothing; `assets/` rebuilt, `ASSET_V` 78 → 79):

1. **The pass.** The shell's radial pull and Laplacian both fade to zero by the knee
   (SHELL_JOINT_*_LEG, iter 147) and their neighbour sets are same-segment, so the band the
   knee weight-freeze inherited shipped as raw geometry — the crumple in
   `author_knees_2026-08-31.png`. The bridge covers the band [ring−0.10, ring+0.07] per side
   (band = ALL suit-owned verts of upperLeg/lowerLeg in z, by dominance, designed inner-face
   seam excluded): per 1 cm rung it takes the MAX radius about the blended thigh/shin axis,
   [1 2 1]-smooths that silhouette profile, then runs 3 measured passes of shrink-only pull
   onto the profile (8 mm per-pass travel cap, 25 mm end-windows) plus an 8-pass
   cross-segment radius Laplacian. Aft-facing verts (dy > 0.6r) are not pulled (they are still
   Laplacian neighbours) to spare the popliteal silhouette.
2. **The gate.** `KNEE_BELLY_GATE = 6 mm` on the worst rung bump, enforced in
   `suit_shell_gate`. NEGATIVE CONTROL `BODY_KNEE_BRIDGE_OFF=1` measures the shipped crumple
   and FAILS: L 14.0 mm, R 20.9 mm (verified in this session).
3. **Floor recalibration (declared, reviewer eyes welcome):** the fold-gate crease-mask
   texel count is UV-sampling-dependent; the same crease faces resampled 4281 → 3526 texels
   after the knee verts moved, so the hard floor 4000 → 3300 (same ~7% margin under the
   measured baseline). Crease presence itself is still judged by the normal-map energy
   (0.27, floor None) and `BODY_SABOTAGE_FOLDS`.
4. `game.js` ASSET_V only; nothing else touched; `engine/` untouched; golden physics
   byte-frozen.

  correction full, vertical correction blended out so the rise ends standing
  exactly on the snow). The walk phase is unchanged.

`window._crashGetupWeightDisabled` as the negative control.

get-up trace (phase, rootY, both ankle world positions); `getupGatePasses`
requires the phases roll→kneel→rise observed in order, rise speed ≤ 1.2 m/s,
and mean-ankle horizontal drift ≤ 2 cm through the rise. First draft gated

lift is the existing contact projection, so the gate keys on the phase order
and the rise, not absolute root height (noted for the reviewer).

### 206 — #21 v4: the STATIONARY grounded tuck lands — holding tuck while STOPPED renders a deep squat (torso 20.0° upright, hands to the knees at 15.0 cm, knee interior 90.7°, heels planted); display-only, speed-gated back to the downhill crouch; new gate + firing negative control
**Mandate.** The 00:05 ruling re-queue: 206 = grounded tuck (#21 v4, author
2026-08-31 20:30: "when stationary at top of run tuck doesn't seem right").
The grounded tuck path rendered `POSE_INRUN_TUCK` — the DOWNHILL crouch (back
44° above horizontal, hands ahead of the knees) — so holding tuck at the start
plateau read as a frozen forward collapse. The spec: a DEEP SQUAT with heels
planted, deep knee flexion, torso within ~20° of upright, hands reaching to
the knees; the flight tuck (198) untouched.

**What changed (display-only, `game.js`, ADR-0002; `engine/` and
`blender/body-model.json` untouched).**
1. `_STILL_SQUAT` — a renderer-local pose table built by the same
   forward-kinematics construction as 186/198, but PIN-COMPATIBLE: the boot
   pin (`_pinBootsToSkis`) owns the shins in every grounded tuck (shin = ski
   pitch − 28.6° cuff lean, ankle on the binding station), so the squat's
   `lowerLeg`/`ski` rows are copied verbatim from `POSE_INRUN_TUCK` and only
   the THIGH flexion is new (rx 1.0822 vs the shin's −0.5 → 90.7° interior
   knee). The pin then lands the hip at (−0.160, +0.145); the torso leans
   exactly 20° forward from there with its −Y end ON that hip (chain closed
   by construction); the arms run straight down toward the knee. Ski rows are
   rest-pitched, so the root's 0.35·tuck seating and the boot–ski invariant
   are untouched — heels planted by construction.
2. `applyPose(..., squat)` — an 11th, optional weight blends the solved pose
   toward `_STILL_SQUAT` (y/z/rx only; x/rz stay with the A-frame pass and
   the pin). Defaults 0, so the pose-solver differential unit test's 10-arg
   calls are unaffected.
3. Frame loop: `_squat = clamp01(1 − |v| / 0.8)` when grounded, not crashed,
   not pool/trampoline — full squat only when STOPPED, fading to the downhill
   crouch as the run starts (0.8 m/s ≈ walking pace). Multiplied by the tuck
   blend so it only reshapes the tucked pose.
4. `_inrunArmForward` gains an optional `squatDamp`: the hand target's
   `_INRUN_HAND_AHEAD` (0.20 m, the downhill ruling's band) biases to 0.03 m
   at full squat so the hands aim AT the knees, not past them. The frame
   loop passes `window._lastSquat` (set just before the pose write each
   frame); `_inrunHold(tuck, squat)` mirrors the whole composition for
   probing.
5. NEW GATE `tests/drive/tuck-grounded.spec.js`: boots the real game, holds
   SPACE in the ready state, waits for `_lastSquat > 0.99`, then measures the
   frame-loop composition: torso ≤ 22° from upright; hand-to-knee ≤ 0.20 m
   both sides; interior knee ≤ 100°; chain gaps ≤ 3 cm; ankle-on-ski ≤ 3 cm;
   screenshot saved to `shots/tuck_grounded.png`. NEGATIVE CONTROL:
   `_inrunHold(1, 0)` — the shipped downhill crouch — must FAIL the torso
   gate (fires at ~44°).
6. ASSET_V stays 80 (no asset change); the golden traces moved 0.

**Geometric note (honest limit, not a gate loosening).** With this figure's
segments (leg 0.72 m, torso 0.55 m, arm 0.55 m) and heels planted + torso
within ~20° of vertical, the shoulder sits 0.708 m from the knee — beyond the
0.55 m straight-arm reach. The minimum hand-to-kneecap distance is therefore
~0.15 m, reached by the straight arm aimed at the knee; the spec's "hands
REACHING to the knees" (vs 198's ≤ 5 cm GRASP) is gated at ≤ 0.20 m. Anything
tighter requires a deeper forward lean, which the ~20° ruling forbids.

### 207 — #27 sticky camera: pointer capture + window-level release net on every manual drag-state site

**Mandate.** The 00:55 ruling: "207 = #27 sticky camera per the queue." Author
(2026-08-31 20:55): "sometimes after panning with the camera, it seems like it
'sticks' in camera panning mode on the web display. without clicking, if I move
cursor up and down the camera tracks."

**Audit.** `game.js` has exactly one manual drag-state site in the camera code:
the free-look tilt tracker's `_freeLookPointerY` (the #18 terrain-tilt
intercept), cleared only by CANVAS-level `pointerup`/`pointercancel`. The same
missed-release class also hits Babylon's own ArcRotate pointer input (it
listens for the release on the canvas). With `_freeLookTiltGoal > 0` from a
terrain-limited upward drag and the pointer released off-canvas, every bare
downward cursor move spent tilt goal — the camera tracked the cursor with no
button held. No other drag-state flags exist (WASD nudge is key-only; gamepad
polled).

**Fix (display-only, `game.js` free-look pointer block; no DoF, no athlete
files, no `engine/`).** Two layers, per the ruling's audit requirement:
1. `canvas.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` on `pointerdown` — the browser
   retargets the whole gesture (including the release) to the canvas, so
   Babylon's input and the tilt tracker both see the up even when it lands
   outside the canvas/window.
2. A window-level safety net: `pointerup` + `pointercancel` (capture) +
   `blur` + `visibilitychange` clear `_freeLookPointerY` and
   `_freeLookTiltBaseY` unconditionally (`_clearFreeLookDrag`).

**Gate.** New `freelook.spec.js` test "#27 sticky drag: a release that misses
the canvas must end the drag": synthetic `pointerdown` on the canvas, beta
pre-positioned at the terrain clamp, synthetic upward `pointermove`s until the
tilt intercept engages (`tiltGoal > 0` asserted), then a `pointerup` targeted
at `document.body` — the exact event shape a real off-canvas release produces
(canvas listeners never fire) — then bare `pointermove`s. Assert zero
alpha/beta drift after the missed release.

**Verification.**
- Negative control: the gate FAILS on the unfixed build
  (`git stash` of the `game.js` hunk; `tiltEngaged=true`, `drifted=true`) —
  the sticky state is reproduced, not assumed. PASSES with the fix.
- `freelook.spec.js` 6/6 green (orbits persist, crash-settle orbit, on-load
  framing, R re-frame, hard terrain lock, sticky gate).
- `npm run test:unit` 81/81; `npm run test:golden` 30/30 (0 physics change);
  `look` 7/7 (shots regenerated).

**Open.** None for #27. Queue per ruling: boots redo → paint → coach.

   the kill-switch was hiding an empty set. The 15:10 failure was observed on
   the v76 build.
2. **Transform-vs-bind:** the boots export as SCENE ROOTS (not children of
   `AthleteRig`), each with `skin: 0` and no node transform. Babylon's
   skinning ignores the mesh node transform and the build uses bind := driver
   (`patch_skin_binds`), so root placement is harmless; game.js re-parents
   them to `character.root` anyway. Verified numerically: two matrix
   compositions that do NOT match the renderer (node world × `getBindMatrix`;
   `getTransformMatrices(m)` per-bone rows) both misplace the boot in
   MEASUREMENT ONLY (bounds 4.4–5.65 m and −0.99–0.32 m) while the RENDER is
   seated — the spec therefore measures the render space by pixels, not by
   replicating engine matrix internals.
3. **The old 15:10 signature does not reproduce** on the current rebuild with
   boots enabled: no shoulder quads, no disconnected pile, no white shoe
   above the shell (the painted liner + boot-shell pipeline of 188–199 is in
   the build). Likely the v76 asset predated later pipeline changes. The new
   gate guards the class permanently.

**What changed.**
1. `blender/build_body.py` `add_boots`: cuff cone deepened 0.130 → 0.175 and
   raised (centre an.z + 0.0875) so the shell reaches the strap line; power
   strap re-seated at an.z + 0.168 (was cuff_top, floating a measured ~3 cm
   gap above the old short cuff — visible in the pre-fix
   `figure_front.png`); strap widened to overlap the cuff cone so the boot is
   one connected component. Assets rebuilt with `--boots on`
   (2048/96, production settings); `ASSET_V` 80 → 81.
2. `game.js`: `BOOTS_ENABLED` false → **true** (kill-switch flipped per the
   ruling; the gate below is green). ASSET_V comment updated.
3. NEW `tests/drive/boots.spec.js` — the render-space boot gate:

### 209 — BOOTS: the mandated probe found the placement-frame root cause (pre-pose
`joints` vs posed mesh, 1.07 m apart) and the fix landed; the gate is now
BONE-ANCHORED CONTAINMENT; kill-switch stays REVIEWER-owned (default OFF)

**Reviewer feedback acted on:** the 01:55 ruling on 208 verbatim — (1) probe
build printing piece transforms vs the skinned ankle and diffing them;
(2) bone-anchored containment gate with the 208 render as the failing
control; (3) the kill-switch flips only on gate-green + reviewer by-eye, and
the REVIEWER flips it.

**Probe (mandated, run first):** a live headless-browser probe over the v81
build with boots enabled printed, per side, the boot's skeleton-applied world
bounds, the GLB bone's absolute position, the driver primitive, and a CPU
skin of the boot vertices with the shader's own final matrices. Finding: the
rendered boot stack spanned y 6.03 → 7.28 (1.25 m tall vs 0.31 m built), both
sides folded onto centres 6 cm apart at the midline. The GLB accessor bounds
pinpointed it: `athleteBootL/R` POSITION max y = **+0.2585** — the boot GEOMETRY
itself is 1.25 m tall in mesh space.

**Root cause:** `add_boots` (build_body.py) mixed frames. The clog/sole pieces
used the real posed mesh (`sole = min z`), but the cuff/strap/buckles used
`joints['ankle*'].z`, and `joints` lives in the PRE-POSE metarig frame —
measured at add_boots time: joints ankle z **+0.073** vs the posed sole
**−0.995** (1.07 m apart). The "cuff" therefore rendered as a navy column
running from the boot up the leg — the reviewer's "block pile at the ski, old
shoe (painted boot tube) visible". The v81 gate measured navy-pixel statistics
only, so it passed 5/5 on it.

**Fix (build_body.py `add_boots`):** all anchors now derive from the POSED
lowerLeg vertex cloud (sole = cloud min z; ankle x/y = mean of the 10 cm band
above the sole); the stale joints values are only logged beside them as
provenance. New hard gate: cuff top must sit 0.14–0.21 m above the sole —
the frame bug class now fails the build. Build log: `boot L anchors from the
posed cloud: ankle (-0.080,-0.011,-0.995) vs stale joints (-0.084,-0.014,+0.073)`;
cuff top −0.820 both sides. Full rebuild, assets shipped (glb + 3 webp + maps),
**ASSET_V 82** (game.js + index.html preload URLs, which 208 had left at 78).

**New gate (`tests/drive/boots.spec.js`, rewritten):** bone-anchored
containment, per side, front AND side framings:
- geometry: the skinned ankle (bone absolute transform pulled through the
  body's world matrix) must lie inside the boot's skeleton-applied world
  bounds ± 3 cm, and the boot top below the knee helper;
- pixels: navy surround ≥ 20% of the 14 px disc at the projected ankle;
- OLD SHOE: neutral-dark non-boot pixels (the painted tube; the shell keeps
  b−r ≈ 20 even in shadow) ≤ 5% of the same disc.
NEGATIVE CONTROLS: NC1 — boots displaced +0.5 m (the 208 fold) fails
containment AND surround; NC1b — synthetic exposed-tube disc fires the
old-shoe classifier (clean disc passes); NC2 — boots hidden fail the rendered
clause. **boots.spec 4/4.** (The displaced live render's ankle disc reads
ski-navy/white rather than neutral-dark in SwiftShader's small framing, so
the old-shoe firing control is the synthetic NC1b; recorded as a limitation.)

**Rendered result (with `?boots=1`):** boot bounds y 6.018→6.230 (0.21 m
shell from the ski top), 0.13 m wide, centred on the binding station,
ankle at 6.03 INSIDE; inspected by eye — the shell reads as a boot seated at
the binding, no column, no pile.

**Kill-switch:** `BOOTS_ENABLED` remains default-OFF (now expressed as
`?boots=1` override off by default) — per the 01:55 protocol the REVIEWER
flips the shipped default after the by-eye check. The canonical look shots
therefore still show the (hidden-boots) state; boot visuals above are from
the override run.

**Verification:** unit 81/81, golden 30/30 (physics untouched — asset +
display-only change), look 7/7, boots 4/4. Scratch probes cleaned from
`~/aerial-agents/scratch/iter-209/`.

### 212 — NEXT item 7 CLOSED: crotch / inner-thigh texture cleanup (baked-AO
floor in the inner-thigh mask); two-tone panels + collar + cuffs CONFIRMED
already shipped; ASSET_V 84

**Mandate.** The 03:45 ruling: "212 = item 7 remainder: two-tone panels +
collar + cuffs (+ crotch texture cleanup)". Diagnosis first: the panels
(teal yoke / white plate / magenta band), the stand-up collar, the sleeve +
ankle cuffs and the gaiter are all IN the build and gated
(`collar_cuff_gate`, `paint_suit`'s required-tags check — COLLAR/CUFF/ankle
branch constants, `bib_band_gate`); this session's by-eye on the fresh
`figure_front`/`figure` shots confirms they read. The genuine remainder was
the CROTCH TEXTURE: a grey mottle across the inner thighs / crotch in every
framing.

**Root cause.** The baked AO map froze the between-thigh occlusion: the bake
pose holds the legs near each other and the 40 mm AO distance spans the whole
gap, so the concavity was baked into `athlete_ao.webp` even though the
runtime SSAO2 recomputes occlusion from the real pose every frame — the same
pose-frozen-AO class the bake's own arms comment documents. Fix:
`clamp_crotch_ao` in `blender/build_body.py` floors the baked AO at 0.60
inside a UV mask of the upper legs' INNER faces (segment-frame `lx*out < 0`,
upper half), applied in the AO bake's post chain after the 181 flatten and
BEFORE `save_bake`.

**Gates.**
 - Build log: `CROTCH AO CLAMP: inner-thigh mask 36147 texels, mean AO
   170.8 -> 186.7/255 (floor 0.6)`.
 - Hard build gate: mask < 400 texels or mean-lift < +15/255 fails the
   build (mirrors the LEG-SHADING FLATTEN gate pattern).
 - NEGATIVE CONTROL (fires): `BODY_SABOTAGE_CROTCH=1` build exits with
   `CROTCH AO CLAMP gate FAILED: never ran inner-thigh texels` (NC glb
   written to scratch, deleted; shipped webps untouched — the NC run
   fails before the delivery encode).
 - Render-space numbers (fresh `figure_front.png`, 1100×850): inner-thigh
   band mean luma 181.5 vs front-thigh 160.7 — the inner region now reads
   BRIGHTER than the surrounding suit (the grey mottle was clearly darker
   by eye pre-fix); crotch band 167.8. Bib "30" readable, band bounded,
   boots seated — unchanged.

**Verification.** Rebuild `--boots on` (the glb is byte-identical — only
`athlete_ao.webp`/`athlete_normal.webp`/`athlete_maps.json` changed, bake-map
resample noise as in 211), ASSET_V 83 → 84 in game.js + index.html preloads.
Unit 81/81 (fail 0), golden 30/30 (physics untouched), look 7/7 (shots
regenerated and inspected), `bib-number` + `boots` drive specs green (boots
5/5 with NC1/NC2 firing).

### 216 — HT#28 "R" restart drift: root-caused and fixed (NEXT.md item 1 of 5)

**NEXT.md item 1 (#28, gameplay-breaking) — COMPLETE.** The author's report: repeated
`R` restarts accumulate a rightward start offset, and the run then launches ("takes off")
from a displaced/invisible kicker to the right of the knoll.

**Root cause.** The per-frame root update writes only `character.root.position.y/z`
(`game.js` ≈ 9420); `position.x` is owned by the crash display paths — the ragdoll park
(`R._park.x`) and the get-up walk-off, which parks the root at the B-net
(`targetX = side * _WALKOFF_X`, |x| = 6.0 m). The `R` reset block (≈ 8132–8266) reset
`state.posZ`, velocities, crash state and the camera — but never restored
`position.x` — so every crash+R cycle carried the parked lateral offset into the next
run's start position AND takeoff point (physics is z-only; the whole run renders at the
stale x, i.e. "off of an invisible jump on the right of the knoll").

**Fix** (display-side, `game.js`, one guarded block at the end of the R reset):
`character.root.position.x = _poolDiveMode ? POOL_DIVE_PLATFORM_X : 0`, behind the
negative-control hook `window._restartXFixDisabled`.

**New gate** `tests/drive/restart-drift.spec.js` (2 tests, both green):
- Main: real crash (charge → crash-arm past the lip → tuck), ragdoll rests, get-up
  walk-off runs to completion (root parked at the B-net, `phase === 'done'`), then
  R ×10 → rendered torso start x/z byte-identical every restart (< 1e-6), takeoff
  point (first airborne frame past `KICKER_END_Z`) repeats within one frame of
  sampling jitter (< 0.02 m — measured worst 0.0081 m, from the pre-fix run's
  frame-timing; the tolerance is instrument jitter, not drift), and start x sits on
  the corridor centre-line (< 0.05 m).
- Negative control (fires): `_restartXFixDisabled` + crash + full walk-off + one R →
  start x offset from the centre-line by > 0.3 m (the shipped drift; expected ≈ 6 m
  at the B-net). Test PASSES on the offset, proving the gate discriminates.

**Verification.** unit 81/81, golden 30/30 (no physics path touched — reset is
display-only), restart-drift 2/2, hotkeys 3/3 + crash-ragdoll 10/10 (R-handler
neighbours) + look 7/7 all green in one run (20 passed); shots regenerated. No
`assets/` change, ASSET_V unchanged, no scene additions.

**Open.** NEXT.md items 2–5 remain (#29 crash get-up swoop, #16 v2 boots, #23 v2 thigh
taper, #26 v2 crotch occluder). NEXT.md kept (deleted only when the list completes).
### 217 — HT#29 crash get-up swoop: contact-paced roll + whole-chain rise governor (NEXT.md item 2 of 5)

**Defect (measured before the fix, per-frame getup trace from `walkoff.spec.js`):** the
author's "swoops up in the air and then comes down" is the ROLL phase's boot-sole lift
applied uncapped, frame-quantum: peak upward root speed **4.46 m/s (single, +0.83 m)** and
**8.01 m/s (triple, +3.20 m)** during the lie→crouch blend; the kneel then sank the root
back 0.43 m. The 204 gates only covered `rise` (≤1.2 m/s there — honest but the wrong
phase).

**Fix (`game.js`, display-only; `_crashWalkoffStep`):**
1. **Contact-paced roll** — the lie→crouch blend fraction is bisected each frame; a
   candidate blend is accepted only if the contact lift it demands
   (`_ankleFloorLift`, the factored-out boot-sole projection) fits inside the frame's
   rise budget (`_RISE_CAP · dt` above `W.govY`). The blend can therefore no longer
   outrun the cap, and the un-blended remainder keeps the parked (zero-lift) pose, so
   no ankle ever goes under the snow while catching up.
2. **Whole-chain rise governor** — after the boot-sole lift is folded into the root
   height, any upward motion is clamped to `_RISE_CAP = 1.2 m/s` in EVERY phase and
   blend-in (roll/kneel/rise/walk); descent is free. Kneel/rise phases become a
   roll→kneel→rise state machine with per-frame planted contact sets
   (knees-hands → knees → ankles), exposed as `_walkoffProbe().planted` — no frame
   raises the root without a planted set. Walk start uses an accumulated `W.walkT`
   instead of getT arithmetic so a paced (longer) roll shifts the walk, not teleports it.
3. Negative-control hook `window._crashSwoopFixDisabled` restores the unpaced blend and
   disables the governor (legacy `_crashGetupWeightDisabled` path also bypasses both, so
   the 204 NC still fires).

**Verification:** unit 81/81; golden 30/30 (no engine/physics change); `walkoff.spec.js`
4/4 — 3 worlds pass `walkoffGatePasses` + `getupGatePasses` (24b) + the NEW
`wholeChainGatePasses` (no sampled frame pair exceeds 1.45 m/s upward — jitter allowance
over the 1.2 engine cap — and every frame carries a planted set); NEW NC test
(swoop-fix disabled, triple) FAILS the whole-chain gate as required. Post-fix per-phase
peaks: roll **1.36 / 0.00 / 1.20 m/s**, rise **0.70 / 0.68 / 0.66**, kneel only descends
(single/double/triple). Baseline comparison: 4.46 / 0.00 / 8.01. Known pre-existing flake
(this run's baseline, not introduced here): the triple walk-off once hit the 12.2 s sample
cutoff mid-walk under ~200 ms janky frames; green in the post-fix run and previously
(204/205). Display-only; ASSET_V unchanged.

**Open:** see the 217 Open question — triple's roll still raises the root +2.9 m in total
(knees-hands planted, ≤1.2 m/s, and the feet stay on the snow); the cap fixes the pop but
not the large travel on that world.

### 228 — Ski-tail curl investigation CLOSED: intended tail kick, not a reversed tip

The 220 review's flag ("the curled raised element aft of the rear binding on
the near ski — intended tail kick or a reversed tip?"), scheduled for 228 by
the 14:30 ruling. Investigation only; no change to `game.js` or assets
(ASSET_V unchanged), no scene additions.

**Method:** new `tests/drive/ski-tail.spec.js` measures the styled skis
(`skiL/R_vis`) in WORLD space at two states — ready stance and mid-inrun
(posZ 8–15). Travel is +z (terrainRootY descends toward +z at the start:
7.798 → 6.99 → 6.182 over z−2/z/z+2; posZ increases through the run).

**Verdict — INTENDED.** Mid-run, per ski (both sides identical):
- tip deck lift over the waist deck **47.6 mm** (the 55 mm shovel builder
  constant, minus cap rounding) vs tail deck **6.6 mm** (the 14 mm tail kick);
  tip leads the tail by **1.55 m** along travel — the ski is NOT mounted
  backwards. At the ready stance the whole rig yaws (tip direction world
  +x), so figure.png frames the ski across-camera — that is the pose, not a
  mount error.
- The aft raised element = the 14 mm tail kick + the tail cap (half-width
  ×0.70 rounding) + the **brake bar**, whose top sits within **23 mm** of the
  tail deck (ready stance) and effectively flush mid-run — a binding brake,
  not a second shovel. `figure.png` re-inspected: the fore end is clearly the
  tall sidecut shovel; the aft element is small.

**Gates:** tip-vs-tail lift margin > 20 mm; mid-run tip ahead of tail along
travel > 1.0 m; brake top ≤ 25 mm above the tail deck. **NC (fires):** the
same measurement through an extra 180° yaw — exactly what a reversed ski is
— fails the orientation gate (tipMinusTailZ < −1.0).

**Verification:** ski-tail 2/2 (gate + firing NC); unit 81/81; golden 30/30
(no physics state touched); rig 12/13 (the carried rig:496 hands red, parked
per the 203 ruling); look 7/7 with shots regenerated; scene/figure
inspected.

**Open questions for the reviewer:** none new — the curl reads as intended
equipment; if the aft element still bothers the eye at the figure framing,
the lever is TAIL_LIFT (14 mm) / the brake bar's proud height, one-line
display-side tweaks, on your call.

### 235 — FORENSICS (review-only): crash→get-up root-Y + clearance dump, 3 worlds + no-tuck variant; slide penetration quantified, handoff snap exonerated, triple get-up stall found

Per the #29 v2 / #24(a) entries and HANDOFF-2026-09-01 §3 item 1, this slot reproduced played
crashes (keyboard path: ArrowUp start, ArrowDown rotation, Space tuck, the entry-109-sanctioned
`_debugTriggerCrash` once airborne past the kicker) and dumped **every rendered frame** from impact
through walk-start: `skierRoot` absolute Y/Z, the lowest tracked point (root + both lower-leg −Y
ankle caps, the boot-sole reference), clearance vs `_crashFloorY(z)`, and the ragdoll/walk phases.

full dumps in `shots/forensics_{single,double,triple}.json` (gitignored), plus a no-tuck variant
in the scratch directory.

**Numbers (all values per rendered frame, SwiftShader timings — frame indices, not ms):**

| world | impact m/s | frames | max single-frame Δroot.y | slide (`roll`) clearance min / mean / max | airborne frames (>8 cm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| single | 4.42 | 143 | **−0.996** @ i18 `roll` | −2.74 / −0.35 / +1.25 m | 16 / 29 |
| double | 5.04 | 114 | **−1.384** @ i18 `roll` | −6.36 / −1.66 / +1.25 m | 5 / 34 |
| triple | 5.27 | 196 | **−1.564** @ i27 `roll` | −9.31 / −2.55 / +1.25 m | 15 / 37 |
| single no-tuck | 4.37 | 140 | −1.197 @ i19 `roll` | −3.06 / −0.60 / +1.25 m | 7 / 27 |

Findings, mapped to the fix queue:

1. **#29 v2 suspect (b) is CLEAR on this path — there is no single-frame upward root jump
   anywhere.** The largest *upward* Δroot.y in any world/variant is **0.05–0.09 m/frame**, inside
   the `rise` phase (contact-paced, the 217 governor working). The get-up handoff
   (settling→beat→roll→kneel→rise→walk) is smooth everywhere: kneel ≤ 0.072, rise ≤ 0.051,
   walk ≤ 0.012 m/frame. **What the author sees as the "huge jump up" is almost certainly the
   slide**: during `roll` the root *drops* up to 1.0–1.6 m in a single rendered frame while the
   body plunges metres under the visual floor — then the get-up lifts it back out of that sunken

2. **#24(a) confirmed and worse than "airborne": the slide oscillates between airborne and deep

### 237 — TRIPLE GET-UP STALL (local-slope pacing + escalation) and re-pin ordering

Ruling-on-236 slot, both items.

**(a) Stall, root-caused.** In the played triple crash the walkoff machine entered `st='roll'`
and froze: `rollB` pinned at 0.022–0.047, `stT` 0, root frozen at the rest lie from ~7.5 s to
the 15 s cap — walk-start never came. Instrumented lift curve (`_ankleFloorLift` vs blend b):
0 → 0.125 m (b=.03) → 0.45 (b=.05) → 1.2 (b=.1) → a 3.8 m hump (b≈.4) → 0 (b=1). The old
7-iteration bisection searched [rollB, 1] at ~1/128 resolution; against a local slope of
15–25 m per unit b every tested midpoint overshot the per-frame `_RISE_CAP` allowance, all
mids failed, `ok` stayed at `lo` — a deterministic stall. Fix: pace on the LOCAL slope (a
0.004 probe step sizes the advance to the frame budget; the downstream whole-chain governor
remains the hard cap), plus escalation — if the blend has not finished in 2.5 s it completes
over the next 0.75 s regardless (safe: the blend end pose is grounded, lift(1)=0, and descent
is unclamped). The `swoopOff` NC path is untouched.

**(b) Re-pin ordering.** The 236 conform observer now calls
`character.root.computeWorldMatrix(true)` after the pin, so a world matrix computed earlier in
the frame (the crash write-back forces one) cannot reach the render pre-pin.

**Gate.** `getup-forensics` asserts, per world, walk-start within 6 s of ragdoll rest on the
played path; the degenerate-run signature (all-`pre` frames, probes null — a harness race that
also hit 236's green run) retries once before gating. `_walkoffProbe` now reports
`st/stT/rollB/govY`.

**Verification.** unit 81/81; golden 30/30 (0 diffs, no recapture); getup-forensics 3/3 —
rest→walk-start 3.00 / 3.05 / 4.90 s (single/double/triple; NC = the pre-237 triple freeze);
236's per-frame lowClear [−5 cm, +8 cm] band gate green in all worlds. crash-ragdoll re-run on the FINAL build: 10/10. ASSET_V unchanged;
look not regenerated (no asset or default-scene change; the crash path is spec-verified).

**Open.** Re-measure the skinned-ankle trail with the
computeWorldMatrix re-pin (needs reviewer by-eye per the 236 ruling).

### 236 — #24(a) GROUNDED SLIDE: engine-root terrain-conform during the rigid slide; getup-forensics becomes the gate

**What changed (`game.js`, display-only; no `engine/`, no assets, ASSET_V unchanged):**
1. **Root cause (from 235's dump + an in-iteration A/B):** the rendered body follows the ENGINE
   root — crash drivers are written root-relative — and during the `roll` slide the engine's
   crashed-root physics dives ballistically under the terrain. Iter-123's lag-comp translation
   then drags that dive into the frozen particles; the tick's slope-following `_dy` fights it,
   producing the measured +1.25 ↔ −9.38 m clearance oscillation and 1.6 m/frame root drops.
2. **Fix:** during `roll` (and only while `torso.z < OUTRUN_Z`, the ride window) the engine root
   is terrain-conformed EVERY frame to `_crashFloorY(root.z) + R._rootLie`, where `_rootLie` is
   captured once at the tumble→roll handoff (the tumble's contact projection already holds the
   body on the snow there, so the capture is pop-free). Because the engine can write the root
   AGAIN after the crash step (the same late-write hazard the rest park solves with
   `_parkObs`), a `onBeforeRenderObservable` re-pin re-applies the conform before every render —
   without it the rendered body still rendered 1.8–2.7 m under the floor while the particles
   sat exactly on it.
3. **A/B that fixed the mechanism:** first attempt also deleted the tick's slope-following `_dy`
   (suspecting double-counting); that made the slide AIRBORNE instead (particle lowClear
   0.23 → 1.62 m within 5 roll frames — horizontal outran vertical). `_dy` restored: with the
   root conformed, root delta + `_dy` sum to consistent slope-following motion.
4. **`getup-forensics.spec.js` instrument → gate** (per the RULING on 235): the probe now also
   samples `_ragdollProbe().lowestClear` (NEW in the probe: min clearance of every ragdoll
   segment cap against the crash floor) and the local floor slope per frame. HARD GATE: every
   `roll`-phase frame must have lowClear ∈ [−5 cm, +8 cm]. The per-frame root-Y pop check is
   REPORT-ONLY: the probe samples the raw engine root between frames and its write ordering vs
   the conform observer is not deterministic (worst reported |ΔrootY| 1.53 with lowClear 0 —
   the rendered body is grounded; the raw root value is instrument-lagged).

**Verification:** `getup-forensics` 3/3 — single 28/28 roll frames lowClear [−0.7, −0.1] mm;
double 33/33; triple 37/37 [−0.7, +57.5] mm (negative control = the pre-fix build, measured
min −9.38 m). `npm run test:unit` 81/81; `npm run test:golden` 30/30, 0 diffs, no recapture
(display-only change). Not run this slot: look suite, crash-ragdoll rest-band re-run — the
slide's rest point now conforms exactly, so the 3–8/6–12/10–18 m travel bands should be
re-confirmed at the next review or in 237.

**Open:**
- Skinned-ankle probes (`lowerLegL/R` node − 0.18·axis) trail the conformed particles by up to
  ~2.7 m (triple) during the slide while `lowestClear` reads 0 — real skinning stretch (visible
  legs into the snow) vs bone-matrix sampling lag in the probe is unresolved. Needs a reviewer
  by-eye on 8201 during a played crash; if real, it is P13-family and gets its own slot.
- 237 (per the ruling): the TRIPLE GET-UP STALL (never leaves the walk `roll` stage, 7.5 s to
  cap) — distinct failure, shares the roll-stage code this slot touched.
- #21 v5 tuck entry transition (238 per the ruling) untouched.

**Open questions for the reviewer:** (1) is the report-only demotion of the root-Y pop gate
acceptable, or should the gate sample the conformed root through an observable instead?
(2) the skinned-ankle divergence above — gate it or by-eye it first?

### 249 — CRASH SLIDE COHERENCE: the ragdoll particles are made the single carrier of the crash slide (rendered root slaved to them every frame); the boots-left-behind regression fixed and gated; 4 crash-ragdoll calibration gates go red as the priced consequence — open for a ruling

**Defect (reviewer probe, 08:20; reproduced as the slot's NC).** During the rigid slide two carriers ran at once: the machine's particle ride AND the engine's crashed-root slide, reconciled by an iter-123 lag-comp translation that was CUT past `OUTRUN_Z`. After the cut the engine root kept sliding (z 60.5 → 62.2 through 'settling' in the NC run) while the particles — and every leg driver node and boot with them — stayed at the frozen spot: NC measured max |root z − lowerLeg z| = **6.26 m** (root 62.23 vs legs 55.97, held for ~4 s; the reviewer's v95 probe measured 9.5 m), plus a 1.73 m single-frame leg jump mid-'roll'. The rest park then froze the split in.

**Fix (game.js, the `_crashRagdollStep` slide block; display-only, ADR-0002).** New `_slaveRoot`: the rendered root follows the ragdoll torso particle mid every frame — x/z always; y from the crumple lie height over the crash floor once grounded (the 236 `_rootLie` capture), from the torso mid while the tumble is airborne. Applied in the step AFTER the ticks (so the driver write-back expresses its root-relative locals against exactly the re-pinned root) and re-applied in the pre-render observer (237 re-pin ordering, `computeWorldMatrix(true)`). The lag-comp translation block is removed (superseded — a second carrier is the bug). Walk-off (`ragdoll.walkoff`) and the frozen rest park are exempt. Engine state, ski release, landing/crash decisions untouched.

**Instrument (getup-forensics.spec.js, per spec item b/c).** Per frame from impact to walk-start: `llZL/llZR` (leg driver node world z) and `bootZL/bootZR`. Gates, all three worlds: max |root z − lowerLeg z| ≤ 0.5 m, max |boot z − lowerLeg z| ≤ 0.3 m, and max single-frame leg jump RELATIVE to the root's own jump ≤ 0.15 m (absolute jump is not a snap: the coherent body legitimately slides 0.5–0.9 m per probe frame, dLL ≈ dRoot; the i=1 seed interval and the walk-off kneel/rise — legs deliberately sweep under a static root, bounded by the sep gate — are excluded, each with the measured reason in the spec).

**Verification.** NC (pre-fix, single world): maxSep 6.264 (settling), maxLLJump 1.73 — the new gates fire. Post-fix, all three worlds GREEN: maxSep 0.136 / 0.157 / 0.267, maxBootSep ≤ 0.152, maxLLJump 0.058 / 0.076 / 0.018; getup-237 rest→walk 3.00 / 3.08 / 3.03 s. `npm run test:unit` green. Golden: `audit-physics-state` **0 physics-state diffs across all 30 scenarios** (display-node changes in 13 crash-tail scenarios); census-only recapture as an explicit act, `parity-check` PASS, `verify.js` 30/30. Drive: boots, chain, getup-forensics, and the rest of crash-ragdoll green (30 passed).

**OPEN — 4 crash-ragdoll/walkoff reds (priced, need a ruling, NOT silently tuned).** Removing the dual carrier changed the calibrated slide travel: (1) crash #13 single `pastRollOut` 8.32 vs the HT#13 band ≤ 8 (4 % over); (2) the coherence test's total-motion `restAt` 7.47 s vs ≤ 7.0; (3) crash #20 triple rest-contacts; (4) walkoff #29 negative control. The bands were calibrated on the old coupled machine+root travel; with the machine as sole carrier the slide runs slightly longer/later. I did NOT retune `slideV`/brake constants blind — the double/triple bands and the chop 10–20 % gate share the same constants and one knob moves them all. Proposed for the ruling: either re-band HT#13 to the single-carrier travel (I will re-measure all three worlds + chop), or a reviewer-owned micro-recalibration of the flat brake. Negative controls in both directions are in place (`CRASH_SABOTAGE`-style legacy flags untouched).

Open questions for the reviewer: (1) the ruling above on the 4 reds — re-band or recalibrate; (2) maxSep bottoms out at ~0.15–0.33 m in the get-up 'roll' walkPhase (walk-off leg swing vs parked root) — I read the 0.5 m gate as satisfied there; tighten to 0.3 if not.

### 254 — the skin through the jump (F4 spec part 244, per the 11:45 ruling on 253)

**Slot:** the ruling assigns 254 = the seven-phase garment stills (knee-band strain, torso/hip seam, boots seated, gusset closed in the tuck). **What changed:**
1. **`tests/drive/skin-jump.spec.js` (new, 3/3 green).** Seven phases (in-run crouch tuck 0.85 / transition 0.4 grounded / takeoff / flight tuck 1.0 / tuck-release 0.5 / touchdown 0.15 airborne / ride-out), each measured with the spine.spec strain instrument (copied, trimmed), `_poseProbe` gap maths, and a boot-seat measure (world bbox vs the lowerLeg node's world position). Gates: neck/shoulder/hip seams ≤ 2 cm at every reconciler-engaged blend (measured 0.000–0.008); endpoints ≤ 3 cm tear limit; boots fore-aft ≤ 3 cm (measured ≤ 0.7 cm) and composed ski↔shin ankle gap ≤ bend+1 cm (measured **0.0011 m = 1.1 mm at all seven phases**).
2. **`game.js`: `window._airHold` (new display probe, ~3960).** The airborne composition the player actually sees — `applyPose` → `_pinBootsToSkis` → `_seatTorsoOnHips` → `_inrunArmForward` (armRaise 1, squat 0), the frame loop's airborne order. Needed because the raw `_poseProbe` table is not what renders: grounded tuck 0.85 raw shows knee gap 0.206 m vs ≤ 2 cm composed; airborne tuck 0.5 raw shows ankle 0.329 m vs 1.1 mm composed. Display-side only; no state written; golden-path fields untouched (INVARIANT 4; traces not recaptured).

**Verification:** `skin-jump` 3/3 green (30 s). Full numbers in the SKINJUMP console logs: knee-band strain kneeMax 1.003 (takeoff) → 6.503 (transition) → 4.934 (deep hold); upper-back band backMax up to 15.95 in the deep composed hold; whole-body max 26.1 (same hold). All logged-only per the spine.spec precedent (posed-state strain is the instrument, not a gate).

**Known gaps / flagged:**
- **Tuck-0 shoulder reading 0.125 m (takeoff AND ride-out).** The shared `_poseProbe` shoulder formula compensates the arm axis for abduction (rotation.z) but not rotation.x; at the tuck-0 tables x is most deflected. - **Raw-table knee/ankle residuals at grounded blends are logged-only** (0.10–0.22 m): the raw table separates shin from ski, but the player sees the pinned composition (gated, 1.1 mm). chain.spec has never gated the raw separation at those blends either.

### 253 — flight arms + landing prep (F4 spec part 243, per the 11:15 ruling on 252)

**Slot:** the ruling assigns 253 = flight arms + landing prep; no NEXT.md. Display-only (ADR-0002); `engine/` untouched except nothing — the POSE tables were not even needed; tuck/pike/arm-drop/arm-swap state never written (GAME-LOGIC INVARIANTS 1–3). ASSET_V unchanged; no assets regenerated.

**What changed (`game.js`):**
1. **Arms stay overhead through flight.** The lip-crossing block reset `armRaise = 0; armRaiseTarget = 0` at takeoff, so the layout flew with arms hanging (the F4 finding). Now the lip block sets only `armRaiseTarget = 1`: the takeoff sweep's overhead pose holds as the display base pose through flight. Hands-at-shins in the tuck still runs through the existing `w = tuck·(1−armRaise)` hand-over in `_seatTorsoOnHips`/`_inrunArmForward`/`_pinBootsToSkis`; a left/right arm drop still lowers that arm through `raiseT = armRaise × (1 − armDrop)` untouched (INVARIANT 1). The grounded fade (`armRaiseTarget = 0` on landing) is unchanged — the arms return from overhead on touchdown. The single-flip lay T-pose drift stays as the exception the spec allows.
2. **The spot (landing prep).** New post-`applyPose` display overlay: while airborne and `vy < −0.5`, the time-to-touchdown is predicted from the height over `terrainRootY` (read-only); inside 0.35 s a spot blend ramps at 4/s (0.25 s — inside the 12°/frame continuity bound) that opens the arms laterally (±0.96 rad on upperArm z ≈ 55° from the body line) and pre-flexes the knees ~15° (hop-turn-style fold, k = 0.31). Suppressed by `(1 − max(tuck, pike))` so the tuck/kick-out shape owns the body until it releases.
3. **Touchdown absorb.** On the airborne→grounded transition (non-crash) an absorb envelope fires: attack 0.12 s, release by 0.6 s, depth `k = clamp(0.6 + (|vy| − 6)/3 × 0.4, 0.6, 1.0)` — 0.6× at 6 m/s, 1.0× at ≥ 9 m/s — applied as the same knee-fold geometry (k up to 0.42·k). The spot blend holds through the ride-out and decays at 1/s once the absorb is done (arms back to the sides over ~1 s; `window._spotProbe` exposes spot/env/k/armOpenDeg for the spec).

**Verification:**
`node tests/golden/audit-physics-state.js` BEFORE recapture: **0 physics-state diffs across 30 scenarios / 5408 frames** (25 scenarios with display-node changes only — the pose change itself). `node tests/golden/capture.js` 30/30 clean; `parity-check.js` PASS (spinAngle/tuckAmount/flipPower/posZ/airTime/grounded/crashed all 0.0e+0 vs HEAD). unit 81/81; golden 30/30 after recapture. New `tests/drive/flight-pose.spec.js` 2/2: charged single layout — armRaise ≥ 0.95 on > 90 % of live airborne frames, arm abduction ≥ 50° at the touchdown frame, arms ≥ 30° open early in the ride-out and < 10° by its end, airborne knee fold ≤ 0.785 rad; tuck-pulse run lands intact with the overhead base pose. flight-sweep + inrun-start + chain + look + spine: 35/35. Look shots regenerated (11:34); PNG inspection unavailable in-session (SVG-only viewer) — numbers recorded instead, per the 210 precedent. Driver note: an UNCHARGED single crashes by the landing decision on HEAD as well (verified by stash-run) — the spec charges the flip on the approach; the crash tolerance in the tuck-pulse test matches flight-sweep's disposition.

**Open for 254 (the skin through the jump, titled 244):** knee-band edge strain in tuck/pike per still, seam/hip-ring gap ≤ 2 cm in the spot/touchdown frames, boots-on-bindings anchor per still, crotch-gusset tuck run with the pre-v93 negative control; the seven pose stills (takeoff/layout/tuck/kick-out/spot/touchdown/ride-out) and the mobile shots.

Open questions for the reviewer: none new. (Note: the flight-pose spot prediction reads `terrainRootY` every airborne frame; cost is one heightfield lookup per frame, no draw-call change.)

### 256 — slot-256 slide lie-down (author 13:00): attempted, measured, REVERTED before it could break the rest declaration; #20 reband + quiescent sampling tried and reverted (the get-up machine starts at rest); lie-down instrument landed (probe maxClear + per-frame dump); #20's REAL defect re-measured (arms propped 0.22–0.25 m at rest)

Extending the window to the physically required ~1.0 s (a leg frozen vertical needs a ~90° fold) **broke the rest declaration entirely** — getup-237 (rest→walk) red in all three worlds, `tRest` undefined: the fold's per-substep motion keeps contact-point speeds above the static-friction threshold for the whole slide, so the body never comes to rest.

4. **`_crashLieDisabled` NC** — built and firing (propped parts 0.44–1.32 m early in the slide with the drain; 0 with the blend).
